summary: Klaus Bruhn was an Indology scholar who earned his Dr. phil. and completed his Habilitation at the University of Hamburg, studying under Ludwig Alsdorf and Walther Schubring. He served as Professor of Indology at the Free University of Berlin from 1966 to 1991.

Klaus Butzenberger studied Indology and philosophy at the University of Munich under Friedrich Wilhelm and habilitated at the Free University of Berlin. He taught at Munich, FU Berlin, and Humboldt University before serving as chairholder at the University of Tübingen (1999–2017).

Klaus Karttunen is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who completed his BA, MA, Lic.Phil., and PhD at the University of Helsinki under Pentti Aalto and Asko Parpola. He held various teaching and research positions at Helsinki and the Academy of Finland.

Klaus Ludwig Janert was an Indologist who studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg and earned his doctorate at Goethe University Frankfurt under Paul Thieme. He worked at the University of Göttingen before holding a professorship at the University of Cologne (1963–1987).

Klaus Mylius was an Indologist and linguist who earned degrees at the University of Halle-Wittenberg and completed his Habilitation at Leipzig University. He lectured at Halle-Wittenberg, Leipzig (1970–1991), Bayreuth, Göttingen, and Goethe University Frankfurt (1996–2022).
Klaus Pinte is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology who studied at Ghent University under Pol Vanden Broucke. In 2006, he served as a teaching assistant at Ghent University.

Klaus Röhrborn is a scholar in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leipzig, Hamburg (under Spuler, Lentz, and von Gabain), and Giessen, later holding professorships at the University of Giessen and University of Göttingen (1992–2003).

Klaus Wille is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He has held positions at the University of Göttingen, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Klaus-Dieter Mathes is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at Marburg under Michael Hahn and habilitated at Hamburg. He directed the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project and served as a professor at the University of Vienna.

Klaus-Josef Notz was a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned a diploma in theology from PTH Benediktbeuern and a Doctor theologiae from the University of Munich, where he served as a lecturer in 1996.
Klemens Karlsson is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Uppsala University under the supervision of Peter Schalk.

Knut A. Jacobsen is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed his PhD at the University of California, Santa Barbara. He has held professorships at the University of Bergen and the University of Oslo.

Kobun Chino Otogawa was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Komazawa University, Kyoto University under Gadjin M. Nagao, and Eihei-ji. He served at the Tassajara Zen Mountain Center, Haiku Zendo, and Naropa University.

Kodo Akino was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Komazawa University and under Keido Ito, Gen'ei Kato, and Bokusan Nishiari. He held multiple leadership roles at Komazawa University and lectured at the University of Tokyo.
Kodo Kawamura was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his master's and doctoral degrees at Komazawa University. He served as a professor at Komazawa University from around 1968 to 2004.
Kodo Nomura was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held a post as a researcher at Taisho University.

Kodo Sawaki was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Senju-ji, Takada Junior College, and Hōryūji Kangakuin, and under teachers including Sotan Oka. He served as a professor at Komazawa University (1935–1963) and abbot of Antai-ji.
Kodo Yotsuya is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed an MA at Komazawa University and earned a PhD at the University of Hamburg.
Koen Wellens is a scholar of Tibetology, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Ghent University under Charles Willemen and earned his PhD at the University of Oslo under Per Kværne.
Koenraad Elst is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned an MA at KU Leuven and also studied at Banaras Hindu University.
